newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA says rate cut reaction huge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA says rate cut reaction huge.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Friday its unilateral cut in its key mortgage rates, announced on Wednesday, had generated a 75 percent increase in inquiries from customers interested in new home loans.

"The response to our initiative has been very strong with our home loan hotline reporting a very strong increase in the number of calls taken, which we expect to continue throughout the weekend," CBA's personal banking manager Alf Long said.
"Many of the calls were from new home borrowers and customers of other home loan providers," Long said.
CBA stunned the home lending market on Wednesday when it cut its key variable home mortgage rate to 7.55 percent from 8.25 percent, its second unilateral rate cut in less than a year.
The bank cut its key variable home loan rate to 9.9 percent from 10.5 percent in May and its home loan portfolio has grown faster than the other major banks since then.
CBA also cut its "no-frills" Economiser mortgage rate to 6.95 percent from 7.35 percent. Both cuts are effective from February 13 for new borrowers and from March 27 for existing borrowers.
CBA's rates now match or are below the rates offered by the non-bank lenders like Aussie Home loans who fund their lending by securitisation.
